ConstituentValidityFloors.description:
D-IMPL-31's declarable floors, whose breach refuses assembly.

Ruled 2026-07-25 as part of the two-granularity TTL reading: *"Product
classes may declare constituent-validity floors whose breach refuses
assembly rather than emitting a product fresher-labeled than its stalest
load-bearing constituent (the mixing-refusal rule, formally footed)."*
The declaration is here; **the refusal that reads it is plan ``15.5-12``**,
and nothing in the registration path consumes a floor, because a
mixing-refusal enforced at wiring time would be a rule applied at the
wrong moment — the mix does not exist until assembly.

Distinct from :class:`FreshnessSLA` and not a restatement of it: the SLA
is the currency the class *expects* of a signal, the floor is the
remaining validity a constituent must still have for the product to be
assemblable at all. One is an expectation, the other a refusal condition.

Attributes:
    min_validity_seconds_by_signal: Per signal type, the least remaining
        validity a load-bearing constituent of that type must have.
        Deployment-declared identifiers, never interpreted here.
ConstituentValidityFloors.title: ConstituentValidityFloors

FreshnessSLA.description:
§6.3 **Freshness SLA** — the per-signal currency expectation (D-IMPL-106).

§6.3 (``docs/CCF_Whitepaper_1-2.md:1453``) separates two primitives that
are easy to conflate. This one is an *expectation* — how recent a signal
has to be before the product may rest on it. :class:`MaxTTL` is a
*bound* — how long the assembled product stays usable once that recency
can no longer be guaranteed. §6.3 calls them siblings rather than
duplicates, which is why both exist here and neither is a respelling of
the other.

**Per signal, not a scalar.** §6.3 makes the expectation vary by signal
and by decision, and warns that collapsing signals of different currency
into one undeclared figure yields an input an agent cannot rely on. A
single number for a product assembled from an end-of-day filing *and* an
intraday blotter entry hides exactly that difference. D-IMPL-106 ruled
the *placement* and left the shape here, recording that no scalar was
ruled in by silence.

The mapping is keyed by the deployment's own signal-type identifiers and
the SDK never interprets one — the opaque-identifier discipline
:class:`~ccf.skills.catalog.SkillRequirements` already holds. This class
therefore ships no signal name and no number (CLAUDE.md §11, CINV-01).

Attributes:
    max_age_seconds_by_signal: Per signal type, the greatest age at which
        an observation of it still satisfies this class's currency
        expectation. An empty mapping is the positive statement
        :data:`UNMEASURED_FRESHNESS_SLA` documents, not a silence.
FreshnessSLA.title: FreshnessSLA

ProductAddress.description:
§6.3 **Addressability** — the address a class answers at.

§6.3 (``docs/CCF_Whitepaper_1-2.md:1465``) commits every product to an
interface an agent can query by name, parameterised by the intent, the
role and the freshness it needs. The section works that commitment as a
path plus a query string, of the shape
``/context-products/{domain}/{entity-kind}/{id}?intent=…&freshness=…``.

**The path half only, deliberately.** D-IMPL-98 ruled that the request
surface is a *typed request contract per product class* and that
addressability and that contract are the same commitment; the query half
of the worked pattern — subject and instant as typed **arguments** rather
than artifact literals — is that ruling's own surface. Modelling query
parameters here would foreclose its shape, so this class declares where a
class is reached and says nothing about what it is called with.

Attributes:
    address_template: The address pattern the class answers at. A
        template rather than a resolved address, because the subject is
        an argument of the request and not a property of the class.
ProductAddress.title: ProductAddress

ProductDiscovery.description:
§6.3 **Discovery** — the registry facts a class is located by.

§6.3 (``docs/CCF_Whitepaper_1-2.md:1463``) puts a registry in front of the
fabric: products are located by the intent they serve, the domain they
belong to, and the capability they offer, and an agent turns a name into
an endpoint at run time rather than at wiring time. The three fields below
are those three axes. ``capabilities`` is the declared manifest §6.3's
worked registry entry carries. ``audiences`` is a fourth, SDK-defined axis
per ``docs/DECISIONS.md`` D-IMPL-135 — see that field's own docstring.

Every value is a deployment-declared opaque identifier. The SDK matches
them structurally and interprets none, so no intent vocabulary, domain
taxonomy, capability list or audience vocabulary exists in this module
(CLAUDE.md §11).

Attributes:
    domain: The domain the class belongs to.
    intents: The decision intents the class is registered as serving.
    capabilities: The class's declared capability manifest.
    audiences: The audiences the class is declared for — e.g.
        ``{"analyst", "investment_banker"}``. **Not**
        :class:`~ccf.projection.plan.Perspective`: ``Perspective``
        conditions Π's view of the graph under a caller's grant at run
        time; ``audiences`` advertises an intended readership to a
        registry and conditions nothing. D-IMPL-135 (Dave, 2026-08-14)
        ruled the axis on exactly this distinction — a role maps onto
        none of ``domain``, ``intents`` or ``capabilities``, and the two
        come apart the moment one role serves several intents.

        Defaults to the empty frozenset, the honest reading of an absent
        ``audiences:`` block — *this class declares no audience* — on
        the same footing as :data:`NOT_DISCOVERABLE`'s reading of an
        absent registry entry. The rejected alternative was a required
        field with every one of the tree's ``ProductDiscovery``
        construction sites moved to supply it, which D-IMPL-136 §10's
        compatibility posture forbids by analogy for a shipped §6.3
        element with no migration path.
ProductDiscovery.title: ProductDiscovery

ServeObligations.description:
What a product class declares about serving — one obligation and one default.

SDK-defined per CLAUDE.md §11; whitepaper §7.6 (the delivery contract and
its validation gates) and §7.7.4–§7.7.8 (Context Debt gating Forced LLM
and Fail-Closed behavior). Ledger rows ``24.5-L-14`` and ``24.6-L-04`` (the
debt figure) and ``24.5-L-26`` (the per-attribute lineage obligation).

**The two members are no longer the same kind of thing, and that is the
point** (``D-IMPL-251`` C1=A, recorded as ``D-IMPL-240`` amendment 2).
``lineage_inputs_at`` is an *obligation*: the one structural serve-time
gate ``D-IMPL-237`` licenses holds the product to it and refuses by name
(:data:`~ccf.products.gates.GATE_DECLARED_OBLIGATIONS`).
``default_debt_tolerance`` is a *default*: Dave's *"a product class cannot
independently withhold otherwise deliverable context because its own debt
preference was exceeded"* — the class value *"can be a declared/default
tolerance characteristic, but it is not itself a policy boundary"*.

**The three debt concepts, which this field is exactly one of**
(``D-IMPL-240`` amendment 2):

1. the product's own figure — *informative*, and applied only as a
   **default** when the caller states no tolerance (worked case 2);
2. the consumer's declared ``debt_tolerance`` — enforced **as requested**,
   looser or tighter, because the consumer owns fitness (``C2=B``);
3. an applicable regulatory or enterprise policy constraint — enforced as
   **governance**, through :mod:`ccf.products.constraints` and never
   through this artifact (*"policy limits are not placed in product-class
   registration"*).

All three reach one place: the Authority layer resolves them into one
:class:`~ccf.products.provenance.EffectiveParameter` carrying the
authority that established it, and
:func:`~ccf.products.gates.refuse_over_tolerance` holds an already-admitted
product to it. Nothing here is a ceiling and nothing here is folded with
``min``.

Attributes:
    default_debt_tolerance: The class's declared ``D_c`` tolerance, a
        proportion in ``[0, 1]`` (the interval
        :class:`~ccf.halflife.assessment.DebtAssessment` already holds
        ``debt`` to). ``None`` is the positive sentinel *this class
        declares no default* — under which no tolerance applies unless a
        caller or a policy states one. It is the effective tolerance ONLY
        when the caller omits ``debt_tolerance``, and it is then recorded
        with authority ``default`` and this artifact's pin as its source.
        A caller's *looser* value is honored, because a class preference
        is not governance. The NUMBER is the deployment's to author in its
        product-class artifact; the SDK ships no default and no threshold
        (CINV-01, CLAUDE.md §11).
    lineage_inputs_at: The TOP-LEVEL payload members that must be present
        and non-empty at serve — the class's per-attribute lineage
        obligation (``24.5-L-26``; the SDK's declared form of what cp-03
        carries as a product gate). The empty set is the positive sentinel
        *no obligation declared*. Names only: which members a class
        obliges is the class's to say, and what those members contain is
        never read here.

**The name moved with the meaning** (``D-IMPL-253`` Q9). Dave: *"Rename
it."* — keeping the previous name, which called this figure a ceiling,
*"after changing its authority would perpetuate the conceptual error we
just fixed."* The field is the same field, renamed at ``24.6-04``; its
hash posture and its sentinel are unchanged. The previous name is spelled
nowhere in ``src/``, ``runtime/`` or ``tools/``; under ``tests/`` it appears
only in the assertions that assert its ABSENCE, so a reader grepping for it
finds those and the dated records that made it.

Both fields are hash-transparent at their sentinels under ``D-IMPL-243``
amendment 2 (Dave: *"``ServeObligations``' two fields at empty True —
empty ≡ pre-phase 'nothing enforced'"*): a model absent at ``13bd250``
whose empty form obliges nothing is omitted member-by-member at that
value, so a class declaring a tolerance and no lineage obligation renders
the tolerance alone.
ServeObligations.title: ServeObligations

description:
A product class's authored governance, minus the pin registration mints (§7.6).

Whitepaper §7.6 (the delivery contract and its class-level governance);
D-IMPL-31 for the TTL anchor, INV-CH7-55 for the assembly mode, INV-CH7-49
for the per-class schema lane. This is the artifact an adopter writes; the
servable :class:`~ccf.products.contract.RegisteredProductClass` is what
:func:`~ccf.products.contract.register_product_class` returns from it.

**It deliberately does not declare** ``max_ttl_version``. That pin is minted
by *registering* the :class:`~ccf.products.contract.MaxTTL` value, and it is
a content hash of what was registered — the same shape D-IMPL-76 ruled on for
the policy bundle's admitted-version set. An artifact that declared it would
be authoring a hash of something it does not contain. This is what keeps
Gate 3 (TTL bounds) meaningful: the ceiling stays an authored artifact value,
the pin is *derived* from registering it, and a product's own ``expires_at``
remains a separately authored number. Gate 3 checks one against the other,
which is only a check while the two come from independent places.

**Why the operator set is declared here.** It lives on the product class
because the product class is already the artifact that declares what the
product *is*, and the operator set an interpretation requires is a property
of the product, not of the code computing it.

**What this field is, under design E2.** It is the Control Plane **claim**
— the value a deployment transcribes into ``lineage.operators_invoked``,
and never into ``execution``. The operator set the *projection* reads is a
second, separately authored document, :class:`ProjectionRequirements`
(``ccf.projection-requirements``), and the two are held together by
:func:`ccf.deployment.binder.refuse_operator_set_divergence`, called
between plan construction and
:meth:`~ccf.projection.engine.ProjectionEngine.execute`. That binder is
where **authorable** drift fails: a one-key edit to either document
produces a refusal, and it refuses rather than repairs, because only the
author knows which of the two they meant. Gate 2 (lineage strict equality,
INV-CH7-47) sits downstream of both, and what it verifies is
**assembly-path integrity** — the claim as transcribed into the Contract
against the engine's execution of the plan — not whether the claim was
right in the first place.

This passage previously asserted that the projection's declaration and the
engine's resolution were mutually independent. They never were, under any
design considered: :meth:`~ccf.projection.engine.ProjectionEngine.execute`
builds ``operators_invoked`` and ``steps`` in one loop over the same
operator plan, so the engine is a faithful transcriber of the plan rather
than an independent witness of it. The ruling of record is
``docs/DECISIONS.md`` **D-IMPL-86** (Dave, 2026-08-05) together with its
**correction of 2026-08-05** for where the binder call belongs; CLAUDE.md
§11 requires an SDK extension to cite this project's own decision record
rather than the whitepaper. The standing AST guard
(``tests/products/test_required_operators_guard.py``) still refuses a
projection that reads the operator registry's own keys — a tripwire over a
convention list of receivers, not a wall.

``min_length=1`` on the operator keys follows the whitepaper's own posture
rather than an ergonomics preference: §7.6 (*Context Products — System of
Delivery*) makes the empty-operator guard the first of the three validation
gates, and its reasoning — stated here in this project's words, because
CLAUDE.md §11 requires a citation by section number and title and not a
reproduction of the text — is that resolving no operator at all is evidence
the graph was never consulted, so a zero-length set reports a
misconfiguration rather than an assembly that legitimately needed nothing.
A declaration of zero operators could only ever produce a resolved set of
zero, which Gate 1 refuses at assembly time. Refusing it here refuses it
where the author can still fix it. A deployment that serves no product simply
authors no document of this class — that is a different thing from a product
class declaring it needs nothing.

Attributes:
    schema_name: Class identity.
    schema_version: The product class's **own** semver lane (INV-CH7-49),
        which is not the artifact's ``semver`` lane. Two lanes because they
        version different things: how the product's schema evolved, and how
        this declaration document evolved. Lanes are never compared across
        classes.
    ttl_anchor: Declared TTL derivation anchor (D-IMPL-31).
    assembly_mode: Declared assembly mode (INV-CH7-55).
    max_ttl_key: Control Plane key of the class's MAX_TTL artifact. The key
        is authored; the version pinning it is not.
    required_operator_keys: Registry keys of the operators the class's
        interpretation depends on. Order is not significant — the engine
        imposes the dependency order (INV-CH7-28).
    accepted_policy_binding_modes: The **accepted modes** of the
        ``policy_binding`` attestation dimension — an unordered set drawn
        from the closed D-09 vocabulary
        (:data:`~ccf.graph.protocols.PolicyBindingMode`), SDK-defined per
        CLAUDE.md §11. A source whose
        :class:`~ccf.graph.protocols.SourceAttestation` reports a
        ``policy_binding`` mode outside this set is refused for this
        class. These are accepted-mode *sets*, not ordered minima: no
        strength ordering exists between ``assembly-stamped`` and
        ``admission-verified`` (D-09's word "minima" is realized as
        unordered accepted-mode sets). The default —
        ``{"assembly-stamped"}`` — is the positive assertion of the
        tier-1 posture every pre-attestation class already lived under
        (the sentinel-default precedent): consuming a tier-2 source
        requires the class to declare ``admission-verified`` explicitly,
        so tier-2 consumption is deny-by-default until a class opts in
        (D-09). ``peer`` is a reference, not a mode, and carries no
        acceptance set — it is pinned into replay, never ranked.
    accepted_lineage_modes: The **accepted modes** of the ``lineage``
        attestation dimension (:data:`~ccf.graph.protocols.LineageMode`),
        under exactly the discipline of
        ``accepted_policy_binding_modes``: an unordered accepted-mode
        set, defaulting to the tier-1 ``{"graph-supplied"}`` posture, so
        ``product-carried`` lineage is deny-by-default until a class
        declares it (D-09).
    freshness_sla: The §6.3 **Freshness SLA** element, per signal
        (D-IMPL-106 option (b), which ruled it class-level and left the
        per-signal shape to the implementing plan).
    discovery: The §6.3 **Discovery** element — the registry facts a class
        is located by (D-IMPL-98, under which discovery is not
        declaration-only).
    addressability: The §6.3 **Addressability** element, path half only.
        The argument half is D-IMPL-98's typed request contract and is
        deliberately not authored here.
    constituent_validity_floors: D-IMPL-31's declarable floors, ruled
        2026-07-25. Authored here; the refusal that reads them is plan
        ``15.5-12``'s, at assembly, where the mix exists.
    payload_schema_key: Control Plane key of the class's declared payload
        schema (D-IMPL-97 ruling 1). **The key is authored; the version
        pinning it is not** — see the class docstring's rule above, which
        this field is the second instance of.
    request_contract_key: Control Plane key of the class's declared
        **request contract** — the typed surface a caller's question is
        validated against, so that the subject and the instant are
        arguments the caller supplies rather than literals authored in this
        document (D-IMPL-98, option (a)). The **third** instance of the
        authored-key/derived-version rule, and ``request_contract_version``
        is absent for exactly the reason ``max_ttl_version`` and
        ``payload_schema_version`` are. The contract itself is
        :class:`~ccf.products.request.ProductRequestContract`, a separately
        authored ``ccf.product-request-contract`` document that names the
        class and lane it serves, and
        :func:`~ccf.products.request.refuse_request_contract_pin` refuses a
        pin onto the wrong class at wiring time. **Nothing in this tree
        resolves this key at a door yet**: D-IMPL-108 ruled that the
        product-resolver seam is widened exactly once, by plan
        ``15.5-15``, carrying the typed request and the authorized
        perspective together rather than reshaping 24 files twice.

    serve_obligations: What this class declares about serving
        (``24.5-L-14``, ``24.5-L-26``, ``24.6-L-04``). Two members of two
        different kinds. The *obligation* — the payload MEMBERS the class
        names — is a STRUCTURAL declaration the serve path enforces
        through the ONE gate mechanism ``D-IMPL-237`` licenses
        (:data:`~ccf.products.gates.GATE_DECLARED_OBLIGATIONS`): members,
        never a payload shape — ``D-IMPL-238`` reads ``D-IMPL-102`` limb 3
        as *no payload gate*. Products do not declare gate TYPES; they
        declare obligations under the one type the SDK ships. The
        *default* — ``default_debt_tolerance`` — is not enforced by any
        gate: it is the tolerance that applies when the caller states
        none, and a caller's own value is honored as requested
        (``D-IMPL-251`` C1/C2, ``D-IMPL-240`` amendment 2). Its number is
        this document's to author; the SDK holds no number. Defaults to
        :data:`~ccf.products.contract.NO_SERVE_OBLIGATIONS`.
        Hash-transparent at that sentinel (``D-IMPL-243``): a
        declaration obliging nothing is every pre-phase declaration,
        so the field is omitted from the canonical form at that value
        and a declared obligation is rendered and versions the document.

**The seven governance fields above all default**, on the
``accepted_policy_binding_modes`` precedent and for the same reason: an
artifact authored before they existed declared exactly what it declares
now, so no committed document is rewritten and no adopter's file becomes
invalid. Each default is a named positive assertion in
:mod:`ccf.products.contract`, not a blank.
title: ProductClassDeclaration
